capitalisationAnalysis.question: does capitalisation enter the colour expression?
capitalisationAnalysis.answer: NO — not directly. Capitalisation never appears in the colour chain.
capitalisationAnalysis.indirectRoute: capitalisation decides whether an AUTHORED occurrence token is matched. Lowercase "zahlen" matches an authored token (role r-verb) and is painted correctly; capitalised "Zahlen" matches none, falls through to the surface-resolved lexicon entry, and inherits that entry’s contradictory r-object role.
capitalisationAnalysis.confidence: STRONGLY SUPPORTED — inferred from the lowercase/capitalised pair diverging on exactly this point; the token-matching step itself was not instrumented

badgeVsColourAuthority.badge: derived from the entry TYPE (Adjective / Verb / Adverb / Particle)
badgeVsColourAuthority.colour: derived from the entry ROLE (r-object / r-letter / r-negation), or from the occurrence role only when the entry supplies none
badgeVsColourAuthority.rootProblem: these are two independent fields on the same entry, and nothing enforces that they agree. Where they contradict, the popup labels one thing and colours another.
badgeVsColourAuthority.classification: B — role; specifically the entry’s own role field, not the occurrence role and not the badge

doesOneMechanismExplainAll.r_object_group: YES for deutsch x4 and Zahlen x2 — all six trace to entry.role="r-object" contradicting entry.type

doesOneMechanismExplainAll.conclusion: 6 of the 7 actionable HCM share one root cause; the letter "a" is separate
